integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A satirical Brazilian street-news report in expressive stylized 3D cartoon animation. Rounded original adult human characters, clear appealing facial expressions, deliberately animated proportions, matte colorful clothing, chunky hands with five fingers, soft warm afternoon lighting, clean readable silhouettes. Not live action. Vertical composition. A peaceful but energetic gamers' rebellion outside a fictional electronics store in a Brazilian city square. No real brand names, real politicians, weapons, fire or injuries. Cardboard placards on wooden sticks, graphics of a graphics card, RAM sticks, a car and crossed-out bills. Main speakers remain large and legible on a phone, faces within the central safe area; crowd in the background. A few big rectangular pale cardboard signs with straight borders face camera in the foreground so final lettering can be composited exactly. Independent hand gestures, crowd footsteps and placard movement. The camera performs a gentle real sideways dolly with foreground signposts crossing faster than distant storefronts; never spins or hides speakers. One uninterrupted camera shot, no internal cuts, no subtitles, no news lower-thirds, no watermark. Only the indicated person speaks at each time; listening mouths remain closed. Spoken dialogue is natural contemporary Brazilian Portuguese with comic indignation, intelligible normal cadence, no invented extra words. Ambient crowd is softer than the interview. Music: none.
This is a second independent interview in the same cartoon reporting style, featuring different original adult people, not a transformation or continuation of the first interviewee. A young adult Black woman with two short hair puffs, purple gamer hoodie and blue jeans stands screen right. A different male reporter with straight brown hair and an orange vest holds a plain microphone screen left. At least six distinct adults behind them carry cardboard protest signs. Pale rectangular signs are large, camera-facing and unobscured near the lower left and upper background, including QUERO FPS NAO DIVIDAS and MINHA PLACA MINHA VIDA; final exact typography is a separate graphic layer.
0.0-3.4s: Male reporter presents the microphone and asks in Brazilian Portuguese exactly <d>[Portuguese] E a memória RAM?</d>. The woman looks at the microphone, raises one eyebrow, then shows a nearly empty wallet without spilling objects.
3.4-9.4s: The woman replies with matter-of-fact comic frustration, accelerating only into the final punchline: <d>[Portuguese] Pra colocar memória RAM, vou ter que vender a garagem!</d>. She gestures with one open hand at the placard showing crossed-out bills. Her face remains visible throughout. The reporter's smile breaks only after the final word.
9.4-12.6s: Protesters laugh once, one woman raises a RAM-shaped foam prop and a man lifts a graphics-card-shaped cardboard prop above shoulder height. They take a small coordinated step forward with grounded feet, not a marching loop. The reporter moves the microphone toward the group.
12.6-15.083s: The crowd ends with one strong clear chant exactly <d>[Portuguese] Mais FPS! Menos boleto!</d>. The lead woman joins the final chant and raises her cardboard placard. Last syllables finish before 14.7s, ongoing placard sway and one satisfied head nod through the final frame. No frozen tail, extra line or duplicated people.
overall_soundscape: Clean native Brazilian Portuguese, adult male reporter and adult female interviewee, dry comic timing; the crowd is quiet during the interview and clearly audible only on the final group chant. Soft footsteps, cardboard rustle and street ambience, no music and no sirens.
non_diegetic_music: None.
